identity.title: Evidence for Multiple Orbiting Hotspots in the 340 GHz Variability of Sgr A*

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyzed 11 epochs of archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) data to investigate flux density variability of Sgr A* at $340\,\mathrm{GHz}$.

question.value: Does the 340 GHz light curve of Sgr A* show periodic variability from orbiting hotspots, and can multiple decaying hotspots explain it?

evidence.quote: We find that the variability is well described by a model involving multiple orbiting hotspots with decaying emission.
during ALMA Cycle 3 (project 2015.1.01080.S; PI: M. Tsuboi)
(2) frequency band 7, and (3) integration time exceeding 1 hour.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four spectral windows analyzed; detrended light curve at 337.5 GHz

evidence.quote: These features are consistently observed in all four analyzed spectral windows (SpWs).

time_on_source.value: 11 epochs, 35 to 150 min each, total about 14 hours

evidence.quote: each with observation durations ranging from 35 to 150 minutes
The total observing time amounts to about 14 hours.
we focus on the light curve obtained on 2016 August 31 during ALMA Cycle 3

method.value: Calibrate, self-calibrate and CLEAN archival Band 7 data; light curves binned to ~1 min for 11 epochs

evidence.quote: All data were binned with a time resolution of $\sim$ 1 minute.

method.value: Gaussian Process Regression with RBF kernel, correlation length 300 min, measurement errors as white noise

evidence.quote: The correlation length in RBF kernel was fixed to 300 min

validation.value: Matérn kernel gives qualitatively consistent results; detrending other epochs introduces no artificial periodicity

evidence.quote: We verified that applying the same detrending procedure to other epochs does not introduce artificial periodic features.

method.value: Generalized Lomb-Scargle periodogram; FAP from 10^5 simulated light curves with red noise (PSD ∝ f^-2) plus white noise

evidence.quote: estimated using $10^5$ simulated light curves that incorporate both red noise, assuming a power spectral density of PSD$\propto f^{-2}$
We adopt a false alarm probability (FAP) of $< 1.35 \times 10^{-3}$

method.value: Two sinusoids with Gaussian decaying amplitudes and sigmoid emergence of 2nd hotspot, fitted by MCMC

assumptions.value: Gaussian decay form is phenomenological and not unique

evidence.quote: We note that this choice is not unique, and the inferred parameters may depend on the assumed functional form.

findings_qualitative.value: Only one of 11 light-curve segments shows variability consistent with orbital motion

evidence.quote: only one out of 11 light-curve segments shows variability consistent with orbital motion

claims.hypothesis: Periodic peaks in the 340 GHz light curve are statistically significant
claims.experiment: GLS periodogram with FAP from red+white noise simulations
claims.result: Significance falls from 25.4/12.7 sigma to 2.9/0.9 sigma

evidence.quote: We therefore do not regard these periodicities as statistically significant detections.

claims.hypothesis: Multiple decaying orbiting hotspots describe the light curve
claims.experiment: MCMC fit of two decaying sinusoids
claims.result: T1=50.4, T2=30.6 min; sigma1=70.3, sigma2=37.7 min
claims.finding: Variability is well described by the model

evidence.quote: We find that the variability is well described by a model involving multiple orbiting hotspots with decaying emission.

claims.experiment: Compare t_syn with decay timescales and spectral index change
claims.result: t_syn ~150 min exceeds decay times; alpha decreases ~0.4
claims.finding: Synchrotron cooling alone cannot explain decay

evidence.quote: suggests that synchrotron cooling alone cannot account for the observed decay.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Matérn kernel tested for detrending; results qualitatively consistent

evidence.quote: we also tested a Matérn kernel with similar characteristic length scales.

limitations_admitted.value: Fit decay timescales are approximate because of limited light-curve duration

evidence.quote: these values should be regarded as approximate constraints

referee_caveats_inferred: Periodicities are below 3 sigma with red noise, so the hotspot model is weakly supported
Single epoch used to fit a many-parameter model; no model comparison against red-noise-only or single-hotspot
Gaussian decay and sinusoid forms are ad hoc
GPR correlation length fixed at 300 min may affect detrending of 150 min data
